Vérifier le code réellement mesuré de la variante T1 à blocs de 16 pixels avant de décider si cette alternative d’ordonnancement mérite une intégration avec Gm1.

Gm1 est la base correcte la plus rapide (0,358794 s; score 0,906925). Tester une seule interaction: remplacer son ordonnancement dynamique par blocs de 64 par celui à blocs de 16 de T1, tout en conservant le SoA et les intersections de Gm1. Le résultat T1 à blocs de 16 est valide, mais un peu plus lent que le meilleur T1 seul; le bénéfice combiné est donc incertain. Préserver la génération de graine et les flux RNG de Gm1, sans reprendre le réensemencement global de T1. Ne pas intégrer T2: ses variantes n’ont pas montré de gain et Gm1 accumule déjà une valeur locale par pixel.

L’intégration 68c82b80512f4deb est correcte, mais son temps moyen (0,359474 s) est légèrement supérieur à celui de Gm1 (0,358794 s), sans gain établi. Les alternatives restantes n’offrent pas une hypothèse assez forte pour justifier une autre intégration: T2 est proche du baseline et Gm1 accumule déjà une valeur locale par pixel. Je termine sans déclarer de confirmation indépendante; retenir le meilleur programme vérifié puis le confirmer.

children.objective: Explore OpenMP parallelization of independent pixels or scanlines in src/candidate.cpp, with the requested `threads` as a hard maximum and no writes shared between workers. Replace the shared `drand48` state with a suitable per-logical-sample or per-pixel independent uniform PRNG stream so scheduling and thread count cannot introduce races or reuse correlated streams. Preserve the existing ray math and sample counts: nsubsamples squared primary rays and all 64 ambient rays at each hit. Compare sensible loop granularities/schedules, including the 1-core case, and report correctness plus repeated timings for every official performance configuration. Do not alter other files or the ABI.
children.subject: Thread-safe OpenMP pixel parallelism and independent sampling

children.objective: Optimize only the scalar primary-ray/per-pixel path in src/candidate.cpp, leaving the ambient-occlusion ray-generation/intersection kernel, RNG sequence, and thread scheduling unchanged. Measure invariant hoisting and local scalar accumulation/write-once changes separately against the original, then measure their combination; do not assume combined gains are additive. Preserve geometry and all primary samples, and check any rounding changes against the required RMSE and absolute-mean thresholds. Run all official correctness cases and repeated timings at each performance configuration so the result remains useful when considered for integration with the other tracks.
children.subject: Isolated scalar primary-ray and pixel-output experiments

children.objective: Investigate ambient-ray generation and intersection throughput in src/candidate.cpp while keeping this separate from primary-ray traversal and OpenMP scheduling. Contrast the cost of scalar direction generation (for example, paired sin/cos only if supported by the frozen build) with batched/compiler-vectorized or intrinsic sphere/plane intersections; measure isolated variants before combinations. Preserve the uniform independent sampling distribution, random consumption where possible, all 64 rays per hit, geometry, and hit/root conditions. Do not use early-outs that omit required intersection work or unverified ISA instructions; retain a build-valid fallback if needed and do not inspect the runtime environment. Report correctness and repeated timings for all official configurations, including nsubsamples=3.
children.subject: Ambient-ray generation and intersection throughput

Measure invariant hoisting and local scalar accumulation/write-once changes separately against the original, then measure their combination; do not assume combined gains are additive. Preserve geometry and all primary samples, and check any rounding changes against the required RMSE and absolute-mean thresholds. Run all official correctness cases and repeated timings at each performance configuration so the result remains useful when considered for integration with the other tracks.
children.subject: Isolated scalar primary-ray and pixel-output experiments

children.objective: Investigate ambient-ray generation and intersection throughput in src/candidate.cpp while keeping this separate from primary-ray traversal and OpenMP scheduling. Contrast the cost of scalar direction generation (for example, paired sin/cos only if supported by the frozen build) with batched/compiler-vectorized or intrinsic sphere/plane intersections; measure isolated variants before combinations. Preserve the uniform independent sampling distribution, random consumption where possible, all 64 rays per hit, geometry, and hit/root conditions. Do not use early-outs that omit required intersection work or unverified ISA instructions; retain a build-valid fallback if needed and do not inspect the runtime environment. Report correctness and repeated timings for all official configurations, including nsubsamples=3.
children.subject: Ambient-ray generation and intersection throughput
